title: Browser native capabilities lab
lead1: Many needs require no library: fullscreen, wake lock, geolocation, notifications, sharing, and network detection are built in. Here they are wrapped into Hooks exposing a
lead2: field — when unsupported it explains clearly instead of doing nothing. The capability-detection logic lives in
lead3: as pure functions, covered by unit tests.
capHint: Results vary by browser: Safari added Wake Lock late, Network Information is mostly Chromium, and geolocation & clipboard need a secure context (HTTPS or localhost).
fsTitle: ① Fullscreen: put any element fullscreen
fsExitHint: Press Esc or click again to exit
fsEnterHint: Click below to fullscreen this area
wakeHint: Great for demo walls, monitoring dashboards, and recordings. Switching tabs auto-releases the lock; returning to the foreground requires re-requesting.
wakeUnsupported: This browser does not support Screen Wake Lock (older Safari / insecure context)
geoHint: The browser pops an auth prompt; denial or non-HTTPS both fail. The error is passed straight back, not swallowed.
geoUnsupported: Geolocation is unsupported in this environment
notifyBody: This is a native browser notification
notifyHint: Permission has three states: granted / denied / prompt. After denial you can only guide the user to browser settings; code cannot re-prompt.
shareVibHint1: Share and vibrate are mostly unavailable on desktop (
shareVibHint2: will be false); they work best on mobile.
netTitle: ⑥ Network info: degrade loading by connection speed
netUnsupportedHint: This browser does not support the Network Information API (mostly Chromium).
netScenario: Practical use: on weak networks (2g / saveData), degrade to low-res images, disable autoplay, and defer non-critical requests.
